title: Get firewall, VPN and iLO/iDRAC management interfaces off the internet
summary: This month's exploited flaws in Cisco ASA/FTD and FortiMail hit internet-facing edge devices. CISA's directive BOD 23-02 sets a clear baseline: management interfaces of routers, switches, firewalls, VPN concentrators, proxies, load balancers and out-of-band server management (iLO, iDRAC) should not be reachable from the public internet.
steps: Build an inventory of edge and management interfaces. Scan your public IP ranges from outside for management protocols (HTTPS/HTTP, SSH, Telnet, SNMP, RDP, SMB, VNC and similar), as BOD 23-02 lists.

For each exposed interface, either make it reachable only from an internal, preferably isolated, management network, or put it behind an access-control enforcement point that is separate from the device itself (Zero Trust). CISA prefers the second option.
Make it stick: add a control so that newly deployed devices can't come up with management exposed. Use a change-template check plus recurring external scans.
Subscribe to your edge vendors' PSIRT feeds and to the CISA KEV catalog, and treat KEV entries for edge devices as emergency changes.
Separate the VPN user service from device management. A VPN portal has to be public; its admin interface doesn't.
pitfalls: BOD 23-02 is mandatory only for US federal civilian agencies, but CISA publishes it as guidance others can use.
The directive doesn't cover cloud provider management portals and APIs. Protect those with identity controls instead.
The 14-day remediation window in BOD 23-02 is a federal requirement, not a vendor recommendation. Use it as a benchmark.

sources.title: CISA BOD 23-02: Mitigating the Risk from Internet-Exposed Management Interfaces
